A.explanation: Power is $P = Fv$ when force and velocity are parallel, so with $v$ known the wind force $F$ gives work per unit time.

B.explanation: Distance per unit time is speed, which is already given as $v$, so it adds no new information.

C.explanation: Total energy input without the time taken cannot give energy per unit time, which is power.

D.explanation: Weight acts vertically while motion is horizontal, so it does no work in the direction of $v$ and cannot give wind power.

hints: Notice the phrase work done per unit time - this is the definition of power $P$ measured in $\text{W}$.
The wind force and the velocity $v$ are stated to be in the same direction, so think how $P$ relates to $F$ and $v$ for parallel vectors.
Since $v$ is already known, decide which missing quantity in the relation $P = Fv$ would let you calculate $P$.
walkthrough: Identify the required quantity: work done per unit time is power, $P = \frac{W}{t}$.
State the governing rule for a force parallel to velocity: $P = Fv$, because $W = Fx$ and $v = x/t$.
Use the given information: the sailboat velocity $v$ is known and the wind force is parallel to $v$, so $\cos 0 = 1$.
Conclude that $P$ can be found if the wind force $F$ is also known, with $P$ in $\text{W}$ when $F$ is in $\text{N}$ and $v$ is in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
